questions.title: Microscopy and organelles

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Eyepiece graticule.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Mitochondria supply ATP for synthesis/transport; rough ER ribosomes synthesize proteins and the ER transports/folds them.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Both have plasma membrane, cytoplasm, DNA and ribosomes; bacteria lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; bacterial DNA is circular and 70S ribosomes are smaller than eukaryotic 80S ribosomes.

questions.title: Joint hypermobility study

solparts.label: a

stem: Photosynthetic oxygen production was measured under equal photon fluxes of different wavelengths for shallow and deep-water algae.

questions.title: Algal pigments and depth

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: 480 nm / blue light.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Red wavelengths are absorbed by water and do not penetrate deeply; selection favours pigments absorbing available blue-green light.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Expose equal algal samples to defined wavelengths at equal intensity; measure oxygen production/CO2 uptake per unit time while controlling temperature and biomass.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Different pigments absorb different wavelengths; excitation energy is transferred to chlorophyll in reaction centres; a broader range of light energy can drive electron transfer/ATP and reduced NADP formation.

solparts.label: e
solparts.html: Paper or thin-layer chromatography.

stem: Satellite estimates of forest cover and atmospheric measurements were obtained for one tropical region.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Calculate the percentage loss of forest cover from 2005 to 2025.

parts.label: b
parts.html: State one reason satellite estimates from different years may not be directly comparable.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain one way forest loss can change regional rainfall.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Explain how geographic isolation can lead to speciation in forest fragments.

parts.label: e
parts.html: Explain a positive feedback involving forest loss and climate change.

questions.title: Forest loss and climate feedback

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Different sensor resolution, cloud cover, classification method or seasonal timing.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Reduced transpiration lowers water vapour and cloud formation; less latent heat exchange can alter convection and reduce rainfall.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Gene flow stops; different selection pressures/drift change allele frequencies; mutations accumulate until reproductive isolation develops.

solparts.label: e
solparts.html: Forest loss releases CO2 and removes a carbon sink; stronger greenhouse warming increases drought/fire risk; further forest loss releases more carbon.
